_strings.@@03f313fb24cb: Treaty conformity — MI conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MI income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MI return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: MI starts from federal AGI and has no treaty add-back, so federally treaty-exempt income (already excluded from federal AGI) flows through untaxed -> conforms. Confirmed two ways from michigan.gov sources: (1) The 2025 MI-1040 begins at line 10 "Adjusted Gross Income from your U.S. Form 1040" (the 2025 instructions say to copy AGI directly from your U.S. Form 1040/1040NR/1040SR), and Michigan modifications are only the enumerated additions on Schedule 1 (line 11) and subtractions (line 13). (2) The 2025 Schedule 1 "Additions to Income" lines 1-8 (totaled on line 9) contain NO addition for income exempt under a federal tax treaty. The words "treaty"/"treaties" appear zero times in the entire 2025 MI-1040 instruction book AND the standalone 2025 Schedule 1 form, so there is no Michigan add-back analogous to California's Schedule CA treaty addback.

_strings.@@6d9116ac95b6: Homestead Property Tax Credit (general claimants) — Available to Michigan resident homeowners and renters whose homestead is in Michigan and who were a Michigan resident for at least 6 months of 2025. You must own and occupy the homestead (property taxes levied in 2025), or have paid rent under a rental contract. Cannot claim if total household resources exceed $71,500, or if the homestead's taxable value exceeds $165,400 (excluding unoccupied farmland classified as agricultural). Renters: in most cases 23% of rent paid is considered property tax eligible for the credit. Separate, more generous computations apply to seniors, the blind/disabled, and veterans/surviving spouses (MI-1040CR-2 where applicable).

_strings.@@a93a32c016dc: Home Heating Credit (low-income heating-cost credit) — Helps qualified low-income Michigan homeowners and renters pay part of their home heating costs. Eligibility and credit are determined by the number of exemptions and a corresponding income ceiling using a standard-allowance method (MI-1040CR-7 Table A) or an alternate computation (Table B). Claimed on a separate form, not on the MI-1040 itself. NOTE: the specific 2025 standard-allowance dollar amounts and income ceilings were not independently confirmed from a tax-year-2025 official source in this research (the MI-1040CR-7 booklet was not fetched), so the dollar figures are left blank and flagged unverified.
_strings.@@ba847db1369d: 2025 MICHIGAN Individual Income Tax MI-1040 Instructions (MI-1040-Book.pdf) — "For tax year 2025, the Michigan income tax rate is 4.25%"; "the personal and stillbirth exemption allowances are $5,800. The special exemption allowance for deaf, blind, hemiplegic, paraplegic, quadriplegic, or totally and permanently disabled is $3,400. The exemption allowance for qualified disabled veterans is $500"; Line 17 "Tax. Multiply the amount on line 16 by 4.25% (0.0425)". Second pass: the 2025 MI-1040 form itself prints line 9a "x $5,800", 9b "x $3,400", 9c "x $500", 9d "x $5,800", 9e $1,500, and line 17 "Tax. Multiply line 16 by 4.25% (0.0425)" — both passes agree, and the instructions' worked example ($53,000 - $5,800 = $47,200 x 0.0425 = $2,006) confirms half-up whole-dollar rounding.
_strings.@@c7ccf3aa4d24: Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit for Working Families (EITC) — You must be eligible to claim an EITC on your federal return. If you do not qualify for the federal EITC, you do not qualify for the Michigan EITC. Aimed at low-to-moderate-income working individuals and families; the amount depends on the federal credit (which turns on income, filing status, and number of qualifying children). The 30% rate (raised from 6% by the Lowering MI Costs plan / Public Act 4 of 2023) continues for 2025.
_strings.@@c8c1dd544124: 2025 MICHIGAN Individual Income Tax MI-1040 Instructions, New for 2025 (p.2) — Expanded Deduction for Retirement and Pension Benefits: 'The Lowering MI Costs Plan provides more options for taxpayers when selecting the best taxing situation for their retirement benefits. Individuals born prior to January 1, 1967 may now qualify for a retirement and pension benefits deduction.'
_strings.@@df5f502351c0: MI state income tax (2025, flat rate): taxable_base $40,000.00 — which must be the state's own income base derived from federal AGI plus/minus the state's additions and subtractions (NOT raw federal AGI when modifications apply) — with no exemptions or standard deduction to subtract; tax = 0.0425 x $40,000 = $1,70

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: MI-1040 Line 17: "Tax. Multiply line 16 by 4.25% (0.0425)" (Line 16 = taxable income = line 14 income subject to tax minus line 15 exemption allowance; Line 10 starts from federal AGI). Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): disabled_veteran ($500 — Line 9c: $500 qualified disabled veteran exemption (unchanged from 2024). NOT applied by calc.state_tax.); special_disabled ($3,400 — Line 9b: $3,400 special exemption — deaf, blind, hemiplegic, paraplegic, quadriplegic, or totally and permanently disabled. INCREASED from $3,300 (2024). NOT applied by calc.state_tax.); stillbirth ($5,800 — Line 9d: $5,800 stillbirth exemption (Certificate of Stillbirth from MDHHS). NOT applied by calc.state_tax.) This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: CHANGED for 2025: the personal/stillbirth exemption rose $5,600 -> $5,800 and the special-disabled exemption rose $3,300 -> $3,400; the 4.25% rate and the $500 disabled-veteran and $1,500 claimed-as-dependent amounts are unchanged. Exemption amounts are year-specific — never carry them to another year. Claimed as a dependent by another: enter $0 on line 9a and $1,500 on line 9e instead of the $5,800 personal exemption — calc.state_tax does not model this; compute line 9e on the form. Michigan filing statuses are single / married filing jointly / married filing separately ONLY — if you filed your federal return as head of household or qualifying surviving spouse, you must file your Michigan return as single (2025 instructions). The flat rate has no per-status schedule, so this mapping never changes the math here. Michigan CITY income taxes (Detroit and other cities; City of Detroit returns are processed by Treasury) are NOT modeled — calc.state_tax computes the state 4.25% line only.
